method: Real MQTT 3.1.1 broker (amqtt) on 127.0.0.1 and paho-mqtt clients: one per device and the hub. Clients send a username (amqtt queues nothing for anonymous sessions). Twin devices (islab.twin, unchanged) run on a simulator driven by the wall clock x10. Routine 'we're leaving': 2 lights off, 2 thermostats to 16 C, 2 shades close, kitchen window check; the bedroom shade loses power 0-1 s before. Confirmation by later state (CONTRACT.md); resend same cmd_id after 2 s without ack (max 3); offline from Last Will. Loss = i.i.d. drop at the adapter, both directions (the radio hop into the bridge).

params.heartbeat_rule: offline after 2 x 60 s shade heartbeat

limitations: Loopback TCP on one 2-core machine: no Wi-Fi, Thread or Zigbee radio. TCP does not lose messages on a live connection, so loss was emulated at the adapter (before MQTT); QoS cannot recover those losses by design.

Time compression x10: device physics, heartbeats, keepalive and timeouts are scaled; transport and Python scheduling overhead is multiplied by 10 in home-second figures (see part A for the unscaled transport cost).
Keepalive 10 home s (paho minimum 1 s wall). Real devices often use 30-60 s; Last Will detection scales with keepalive.
Heartbeat detection is computed from the measured last message + 2 heartbeats, not waited for.

Matter: data model mapping only (cluster/attribute ids from the SDK-generated package); no Matter controller, no commissioning, no Thread. Home Assistant discovery payloads were not validated against a running Home Assistant.
8 trials per condition: p95 values are indicative.
i.i.d. loss; real radios lose packets in bursts.
